Indeterminable Variables of Clinical vs. Non-Clinical Studies

Annika Kuelpmann

2026-10-07

Indeterminable Values by Variable and Study Type

# select relevant variables from data frame sample_categories
samples <- sample_categories %>% 
  select(article_id, category)

# join procedures_data with samples 
procedures_by_category <- procedures_data %>% 
  left_join(samples, by = "article_id") %>%
  mutate(clinical = category == 1) 

# count the tasks with clinical and non-clinical samples
row_counts <- procedures_by_category %>%
  count(clinical)

# select variables of interest
# count the number of indeterminables for each variable
indeterminables_by_cat <- procedures_by_category %>%
  select(7:29, clinical) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = 1:23, 
               names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>% 
  filter(value == "indeterminable") %>%
  count(clinical, variable) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = clinical, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(count_clinical = `TRUE`, count_non_clinical = `FALSE`) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_clinical = (count_clinical / 53 * 100),
    pct_non_clinical = (count_non_clinical / 53 * 100)
  ) %>%
  select(variable, count_clinical, pct_clinical, count_non_clinical, pct_non_clinical)

# calculate the totals across all variables
total_ind <- indeterminables_by_cat %>%
  summarise(
    variable = "total",
    count_clinical = sum(count_clinical),
    pct_clinical = (sum(count_clinical) / (53 * 23)) * 100, 
    count_non_clinical = sum(count_non_clinical),
    pct_non_clinical = (sum(count_non_clinical) / (53 * 23)) * 100
  )

# bind the total row to the main table
indeterminables_by_cat <- bind_rows(indeterminables_by_cat, total_ind)

indeterminables_by_cat |>
  kable() |>
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)

# number of igts per study type, only used for the check below
total_clinical <- row_counts$n[row_counts$clinical == TRUE]
total_non_clinical <- row_counts$n[row_counts$clinical == FALSE]

# percentages are per igt (53 clinical, 53 non-clinical tasks)
stopifnot(total_clinical == 53, total_non_clinical == 53)

# one row per igt and variable with an indeterminable flag and a grouped parameter label
indeterminables_long <- procedures_by_category %>%
  mutate(task_row = row_number()) %>%
  select(task_row, clinical, goal:n_trials) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(task_row, clinical), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(variable != "n_blocks") %>%
  mutate(
    indeterminable = value %in% "indeterminable",
    parameter = case_when(
      variable %in% c("reward_disadv", "reward_adv") ~ "Reward per Card",
      variable %in% c("loss1", "loss2", "gain1", "gain2") ~ "Gain/Loss per 10 Cards",
      variable %in% c("loss_int1", "loss_int2", "gain_int1", "gain_int2") ~ "Gain/Loss Interval",
      str_detect(variable, "freq") ~ "Loss Frequency",
      variable == "starting_capital" ~ "Starting Capital",
      variable == "n_trials" ~ "Number of Trials",
      TRUE ~ str_to_title(variable)
    )
  )

# grouped parameters are the mean of their constituent variables percentages
# counts are dropped because they are not meaningful for averaged groups
indeterminables_grouped <- indeterminables_long %>%
  group_by(clinical, parameter, variable) %>%
  summarise(pct = 100 * mean(indeterminable), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(clinical, parameter) %>%
  summarise(pct = mean(pct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  # wide format
  pivot_wider(names_from = clinical, values_from = pct) %>%
  rename(variable = parameter, pct_clinical = `TRUE`, pct_non_clinical = `FALSE`) %>%
  select(variable, pct_clinical, pct_non_clinical) %>%
  arrange(pmax(pct_clinical, pct_non_clinical))

# print table with percentages rounded to two decimals
indeterminables_grouped |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("pct_"), ~ round(.x, 2))) |>
  kable() |>
  kable_classic(full_width = FALSE)

procedures_by_category %>%
  filter(protocol == "Bechara, 2007") %>%
  count(clinical)

Plot 1

# long format with one row per parameter and study type
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_grouped %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pct_"), 
    names_to = "sample_type", 
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_type = recode(sample_type,
                         "pct_clinical" = "Clinical",
                         "pct_non_clinical" = "Non-Clinical")
  )

# order variables by their larger percentage so the highest appears at the top
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_dot_data %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  mutate(max_percentage = max(percentage, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(variable = fct_reorder(variable, max_percentage, .desc = FALSE))

# create the dot plot
plot1 <- ggplot(indeterminables_dot_data, 
                aes(x = percentage, y = variable, color = sample_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Study Type",
    values = c("Clinical" = "#31688E", "Non-Clinical" = "#35B779")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Percentage of Indeterminable Values",
    y = "Variable"
  )  +
  theme_bw() + 
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(plot1)

Figure 1 (APS Format)

# long format with one row per parameter and study type
fig1_data <- indeterminables_grouped %>%
  rename(parameter = variable) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(pct_clinical, pct_non_clinical),
    names_to = "study_type",
    values_to = "pct"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    study_type = factor(
      if_else(study_type == "pct_clinical", "Clinical", "Non-Clinical"),
      levels = c("Clinical", "Non-Clinical")
    )
  )

# order rows by the larger of the two percentages with ties broken by the mean
parameter_order <- fig1_data %>%
  group_by(parameter) %>%
  summarise(max_pct = max(pct), mean_pct = mean(pct)) %>%
  arrange(max_pct, mean_pct) %>%
  pull(parameter)

fig1_data <- fig1_data %>%
  mutate(parameter = factor(parameter, levels = parameter_order))

# save the plotted values
write_csv(
  fig1_data %>%
    select(parameter, study_type, pct) %>%
    arrange(desc(parameter), study_type),
  "KuelpmannFig1_data.csv"
)

# okabe-ito orange and blue plus distinct shapes so study types stay separable in greyscale
fig1 <- ggplot(fig1_data, aes(x = pct, y = parameter, colour = study_type, shape = study_type)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(name = "Study Type",
                      values = c("Clinical" = "#E69F00", "Non-Clinical" = "#0072B2")) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = "Study Type",
                     values = c("Clinical" = 16, "Non-Clinical" = 17)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(x = "Indeterminable Values (%)", y = "Procedural Parameter") +
  theme_aps() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey88", linewidth = 0.3),
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)
  )

print(fig1)

# 600 dpi png and svg in the folder of this rmd
save_figure(fig1, "KuelpmannFig1", width = 6.5, height = 4.0)

Plot 2

# long format with one row per parameter and study type
indeterminables_dot_data <- indeterminables_grouped %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("pct_"), 
    names_to = "sample_type", 
    values_to = "percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    sample_type = recode(sample_type,
                         "pct_clinical" = "Clinical",
                         "pct_non_clinical" = "Non-Clinical")
  )

# create the dot plot
plot2 <- ggplot(indeterminables_dot_data, 
                aes(x = sample_type, y = percentage, color = variable)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.8, position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +
  scale_color_viridis_d(name = "Variable") +
  labs(
    title = "Indeterminable Values by Variable and Study Type",
    x = "Sample Type",
    y = "Percentage of Indeterminable Values"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()+
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(scale = 1))  # show y axis as percentages

print(plot2)
